title: Reference-dialog corpus and fidelity spectra for safe batching/cache rollback choreography
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Goal: build a lightweight evaluation layer that ties cost-driven batching/caching recommendations to observable quality regressions and a staged rollback choreography. We will create a curated 'reference-dialog' corpus (diverse dialogs + edge cases) and compute a multi-axis fidelity spectrum (semantic similarity, factuality heuristics, formatting preservation, instruction-following score). The system will produce a compact regression fingerprint per config change and drive automated stage gates: shadow-simulations, small-scale canaries, progressive ramp, and automated pullback when fidelity falls below threshold. This ticket covers corpus assembly, scoring functions, threshold design, and the rollback choreography implementation (both automatic and operator-notified modes).
acceptance_criteria: A reference-dialog corpus of ~1.2k examples covering short/long context, multi-turn, instruction-following, and hallucination-prone prompts is stored in S3 with version tag
A fidelity-spectrum produces stable numeric signals (semantic_similarity, fact_overlap, format_preservation, instruction_adherence) with unit tests and documented normalization
Regression fingerprints are generated for any candidate batching/cache config and show delta vs baseline within 5 minutes of simulation
Staged rollback choreography implemented: shadow-simulate -> 1% canary -> 10% ramp -> full apply, with automatic pause/pullback when any fidelity axis crosses configured thresholds
Operator UX shows the top 3 failing examples, per-axis deltas, and an automated rollback suggestion with links to the exact config diff
End-to-end integration test that deliberately triggers a regression and validates automated pullback and notification path (Slack + Console alert)
implementation_notes: Corpus: combine past support transcripts (anonymized), synthetic adversarial turns, and existing eval seeds. Annotate with intent labels and expected formatting where relevant

Scoring: use a hybrid approach — fast embedding-based semantic_similarity (cosine on chonk embeddings), light-weight entailment/fact-check signals (sparse triples overlap), and token-level formatting heuristics for structured outputs
Normalization: per-model baselines will be stored; compute z-scores per axis to make thresholds portable across models/quantizations
Shadow-sim: reuse our existing routing layer to simulate candidate config without impacting production; collect full logits for the reference set where feasible
Rollback choreography: implement as a state machine in deployer service with clear audit events. Default thresholds configurable per-customer but sane defaults enforced
Metrics: add new telemetry keys (regression_fingerprint_id, fidelity_axis_deltas, rollback_trigger_reason) to console traces for debugging and billing correlation
